boundary_rationale: The row is bounded to the single chazon header verse: “The vision of Isaiah the son of Amoz, which he saw concerning Judah and Jerusalem, in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah.” (web:Isa.1.1). The Hebrew opens with חֲזוֹן֙ (oshb:Isa.1.1, byte tier), a superscription noun naming the seer, his father, and the four-king regnal window, with no imperative, vocative, or divine-speech formula of its own; the next verse opens a fresh imperative summons (“Hear, heavens, and listen, earth”, web:Isa.1.2), which is the row's own seam.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Folding the header into the following summons unit was rejected because the header verse carries no imperative or address of its own and names a distinct royal-regnal frame absent from verse 2.
wj_or_red_letter_considered: not applicable in the OT substrate
device_notes: Both superscriptions carry the same relative clause, אֲשֶׁ֣ר חָזָ֔ה (byte tier at oshb:Isa.1.1 and oshb:Isa.2.1); the two superscriptions share the seer's name and the Judah/Jerusalem object and differ only in header-noun class, the sole discriminator — חֲזוֹן֙ against הַדָּבָר֙ (oshb:Isa.1.1 / oshb:Isa.2.1, byte tier).

boundary_rationale: Opens with the double imperative-vocative summons שִׁמְע֤וּ שָׁמַ֨יִם֙ וְהַאֲזִ֣ינִי אֶ֔רֶץ (oshb:Isa.1.2, byte tier), “Hear, heavens, and listen, earth; for Yahweh has spoken” (web:Isa.1.2), calling cosmic witnesses to the case before any content of the charge is stated; verse 3's ox/donkey analogy completes the witness-testimony frame (“The ox knows his owner… but Israel doesn't know”, web:Isa.1.3). The row closes before the hoy-onset indictment proper begins at web:Isa.1.4.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Merging this witness-summons couplet into the following indictment as one unbroken oracle was rejected because the couplet opens with the witness-summons imperatives שִׁמְע֤וּ שָׁמַ֨יִם֙ וְהַאֲזִ֣ינִי אֶ֔רֶץ (oshb:Isa.1.2, tokens 1-4, byte tier) and the rebellion charge follows within the same verse, making this a summons-plus-indictment preface rather than an offense-free one, a distinct move from the hoy-onset indictment that follows.

device_notes: The heaven/earth witness-pair convention is a recognized covenant-lawsuit opening move argued here from the imperative pairing itself, not from a named riv/din verb (contrast the explicit riv formula at 3:13). A cross-seam catchword recurs at accent_stripped tier: בָּנִים֙ (oshb:Isa.1.2, token 8) and בָּנִ֖ים (oshb:Isa.1.4, token 9) collate at accent_stripped tier, the bare plural noun standing at 8 verses book-wide (sweep: 8 verses, skeleton, token-exact).

boundary_rationale: Opens with the hoy-onset indictment ה֣וֹי (oshb:Isa.1.4, byte tier), “Ah sinful nation, a people loaded with iniquity, offspring of evildoers, children who deal corruptly!” (web:Isa.1.4); this hoy functions as the opening indictment rather than a woe-oracle onset of the kind found later in the book, since it launches a description of the nation's condition rather than pronouncing doom on a named target-class. The row runs through the survivor clause “a very small remnant” (web:Isa.1.9) — הוֹתִ֥יר (oshb:Isa.1.9, token 4) governing שָׂרִ֖יד (token 6), a survivor verb-noun pairing outside the book's four-way remnant family — closing where a parashah setumah break falls (oshb:Isa.1.9, single-witness, tier-3) and where verse 10 opens a fresh imperative address to a new named audience.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Classifying this row as a woe_oracle of the ch-5/28-33 series type was rejected because its hoy targets the nation's condition in general description rather than pronouncing doom on a specific addressee-class, the operative distinction argued for the opening-indictment reading.

device_notes: Verse 4 carries the qadosh-Israel title קְד֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל (oshb:Isa.1.4, byte tier), “the Holy One of Israel” (web:Isa.1.4), one of the book's signature divine-title sites. A setumah break is recorded at the close of verse 9 (oshb:Isa.1.9, single-witness, tier-3 corroboration only, not a boundary driver). A place-name catchword straddles the seam at hinge strength: כִּסְדֹ֣ם הָיִ֔ינוּ לַעֲמֹרָ֖ה דָּמִֽינוּ (oshb:Isa.1.9, byte tier) is picked up by קְצִינֵ֣י סְדֹ֑ם and עַ֥ם עֲמֹרָֽה (oshb:Isa.1.10, byte tier at each site); the Sodom and Gomorrah place-name skeletons stand at 4 and 3 verses book-wide respectively (sweep: 4 verses / 3 verses, skeleton) and co-occur in adjacent verses only here. The pair functions as a hinge across the seam — simile at 1:9, vocative address at 1:10 — rather than as argued continuity.

boundary_rationale: Opens with a fresh double imperative שִׁמְע֥וּ דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה קְצִינֵ֣י סְדֹ֑ם (oshb:Isa.1.10, byte tier), “Hear Yahweh's word, you rulers of Sodom! Listen to the law of our God, you people of Gomorrah!” (web:Isa.1.10), reusing the shema/azan verb pair of verse 2 but redirected at a human addressee named by the Sodom/Gomorrah simile just introduced in verse 9, marking a scene/addressee shift. The row runs through the closing imperative catalogue “Learn to do well. Seek justice… Plead for the widow.” (web:Isa.1.17), where a setumah break is recorded (oshb:Isa.1.17, single-witness, tier-3) before the distinct invitation formula of verse 18.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading verses 10-17 as a continuation of the row-3 indictment rather than a new unit was rejected because verse 10 reopens the address with its own imperative-vocative pair naming a new addressee, a tier-1 scene-shift signal distinct from the general description in 4-9.

device_notes: Verse 10's imperative pair shares the shema/azan root pair with verse 2's summons but in different verb forms suited to a plural human addressee rather than the feminine-singular ‘earth’, a paired structuring device rather than a verbatim recurrence (form-class observation, byte-checkable, not a byte-identical claim). A setumah break is recorded at the close of verse 17 (oshb:Isa.1.17, single-witness, tier-3 corroboration only); verse 9, immediately upstream of this row's own opening, is itself setumah-marked (oshb:Isa.1.9, single-witness, tier-3). A chapter-level lexical bracket, not cross-seam cohesion at 1:17|1:18: the orphan/widow pair recurs with its two governing verbs in inverted order — שִׁפְט֣וּ יָת֔וֹם רִ֖יבוּ אַלְמָנָֽה (oshb:Isa.1.17) against יָתוֹם֙ לֹ֣א יִשְׁפֹּ֔טוּ וְרִ֥יב אַלְמָנָ֖ה (oshb:Isa.1.23) — the orphan noun matching at accent_stripped tier and the widow noun at skeleton tier across the two sites, the orphan noun standing at 2 verses and the widow noun at 3 verses book-wide (sweep: 2 verses / 3 verses, skeleton, token-exact).

boundary_rationale: Opens with the divine invitation formula לְכוּ נָ֛א וְנִוָּֽכְחָ֖ה (oshb:Isa.1.18, byte tier), “Come now, and let's reason together,” says Yahweh (web:Isa.1.18), a distinct speech-act (invitation to settlement) from the imperative catalogue that precedes it. The row runs through the closing formula כִּ֛י פִּ֥י יְהוָ֖ה דִּבֵּֽר (oshb:Isa.1.20, byte tier), “for Yahweh's mouth has spoken it.” (web:Isa.1.20), a recognized oracle-closing signature that recurs byte-identically at 3 verses book-wide, also at oshb:Isa.40.5 (כִּ֛י פִּ֥י יְהוָ֖ה דִּבֵּֽר) and oshb:Isa.58.14 (כִּ֛י פִּ֥י יְהוָ֖ה דִּבֵּֽר) (sweep: 3 verses, byte), all three carrying the ki-form, where a setumah break is recorded (oshb:Isa.1.20, single-witness, tier-3). This same opening seam has its own tier-3 witness too: a setumah break closes verse 17 (oshb:Isa.1.17, single-witness) immediately before the row begins.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Attaching verses 18-20 to the preceding ritual-critique unit as its conclusion was rejected because verse 18 opens with its own imperative-plus-cohortative invitation, לְכוּ נָ֛א וְנִוָּֽכְחָ֖ה (oshb:Isa.1.18, tokens 1-3, byte tier), a fresh speech-act distinct from the imperative catalogue of verses 16-17; the quotative יֹאמַ֣ר יְהוָ֑ה that follows at tokens 4-5 is not itself a discriminator, since it recurs mid-verse inside that same catalogue's block at oshb:Isa.1.11 (יֹאמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה, accent_stripped tier; the bare quotative stands at 5 verses book-wide, sweep: 5 verses, skeleton, distinct from the 5 vav-prefixed narrative-onset sites).

device_notes: The unit is conditional in structure (willing-and-obedient vs. refuse-and-rebel), which argues for judgment_oracle over salvation_oracle since the promise is contingent rather than unconditional comfort.

boundary_rationale: Opens with the qinah-style exclamation אֵיכָה֙ (oshb:Isa.1.21, byte tier), “How the faithful city has become a prostitute!” (web:Isa.1.21), a fresh lament-onset distinct from the preceding conditional oracle. The unit is held together as one row by an inclusio: the two-word designation קִרְיָ֖ה נֶאֱמָנָ֑ה (oshb:Isa.1.21, byte tier) recurs at the close of verse 26, קִרְיָ֖ה נֶאֱמָנָֽה (oshb:Isa.1.26; the two sites match at skeleton tier only (sweep: 2 verses) — identical consonants, differing verse-end cantillation — so the recurrence is named at that tier and not claimed byte-identical), “the faithful city” (web:Isa.1.21) bracketing “a faithful town” (web:Isa.1.26). Between the brackets, verse 24 pivots on the stacked title-and-signature נְאֻ֤ם הָֽאָדוֹן֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת (oshb:Isa.1.24, byte tier), “Therefore the Lord, Yahweh of Armies, the Mighty One of Israel, says” (web:Isa.1.24); this hoy, ה֚וֹי, is a divine self-exclamation over Yahweh's own coming action, not a woe pronounced against the addressee, so it is read as an internal turn within the bracketed lament-to-restoration unit rather than a row-cutting seam. Verse 20, which closes just before this row opens, carries its own setumah break (oshb:Isa.1.20, single-witness, tier-3 corroboration).
strongest_rejected_alternative: Cutting the row at 1:23|1:24 into a separate lament (21-23) and a separate oracle (24-26) was considered, since a petuchah break is recorded at the close of verse 23 (oshb:Isa.1.23, single-witness, tier-3 corroboration only) and verse 24 pivots into its own neum-formula turn at token 2 of 12, after the connective and ahead of the quoted speech; it was rejected in favor of the skeleton-tier inclusio bracket spanning 21-26, which is a stronger, byte-grounded cohesion signal than a single tier-3 parashah witness, and the rejection rests on that bracket alone.

device_notes: Held at medium_low because the unity argument (the inclusio) and the tier-3 division signal (the petuchah at 1:23) genuinely pull in opposite directions; this is disclosed rather than silently resolved. The neum stack at 1:24, נְאֻ֤ם הָֽאָדוֹן֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת (oshb:Isa.1.24, byte tier), stands at token 2 of 12 — after the discourse connective לָכֵ֗ן and ahead of the quoted speech it introduces — and across the 23-verse book-wide census of the signature (sweep: 23 verses, skeleton) it is verse-initial only at oshb:Isa.56.8; the rejection of the 1:23|1:24 rival rests on the skeleton-tier inclusio bracket alone, not on the signature's position. A chapter-level lexical bracket, not cross-seam cohesion at 1:17|1:18: the orphan/widow pair recurs with its two governing verbs in inverted order — שִׁפְט֣וּ יָת֔וֹם רִ֖יבוּ אַלְמָנָֽה (oshb:Isa.1.17) against יָתוֹם֙ לֹ֣א יִשְׁפֹּ֔טוּ וְרִ֥יב אַלְמָנָ֖ה (oshb:Isa.1.23) — the orphan noun matching at accent_stripped tier and the widow noun at skeleton tier across the two sites, the orphan noun standing at 2 verses and the widow noun at 3 verses book-wide (sweep: 2 verses / 3 verses, skeleton, token-exact).

boundary_rationale: Opens with צִיּ֖וֹן בְּמִשְׁפָּ֣ט תִּפָּדֶ֑ה (oshb:Isa.1.27, byte tier), “Zion shall be redeemed with justice, and her converts with righteousness.” (web:Isa.1.27), shifting from the first-person ‘I will’ divine speech of 1:24-26 to third-person declarative summary naming Zion's redeemed and the apostates' fate side by side, a discourse-mode shift read as the row's opening seam. The row closes the chapter at וְהָיָ֤ה הֶחָסֹן֙ לִנְעֹ֔רֶת וּפֹעֲל֖וֹ לְנִיצ֑וֹץ וּבָעֲר֧וּ (oshb:Isa.1.31, byte tier), “The strong will be like tinder, and his work like a spark. They will both burn” (web:Isa.1.31), where a setumah break is recorded (oshb:Isa.1.31, single-witness, tier-3), and before the fresh ha-davar superscription opening chapter 2.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Keeping 1:21-31 as one unbounded row was rejected because verse 27 drops the first-person divine voice of the neum-framed oracle for a third-person summary, and holding 27-31 as a separate closing statement lets the 21-26 inclusio stand as its own bracketed unit; the 26|27 seam itself is argued from this mode shift alone, with no explicit lexical frame marker, so it is held at reduced confidence.

device_notes: The oak/garden withering imagery of verses 29-30 anticipates the fire imagery closing verse 31, forming the chapter's own closing figure rather than a list register; no separate row is cut for it. An adjacent-verse righteousness-root link crosses the row's own opening seam: הַצֶּ֔דֶק (oshb:Isa.1.26, token 11) is picked up by בִּצְדָקָֽה (oshb:Isa.1.27, token 5), byte tier at each site, in consecutive verses — the primary undisclosed cohesion signal at 1:26|1:27. A chapter-level bracket rides behind it: the justice/righteousness co-occurrence object stands at 16 verses book-wide and at exactly 2 verses in this chapter, oshb:Isa.1.21 and oshb:Isa.1.27 (sweep: 16 verses / 2 verses, skeleton); at oshb:Isa.1.27 the form is בְּמִשְׁפָּ֣ט (token 2), prefixed, not the bare noun מִשְׁפָּ֗ט of oshb:Isa.1.21 (token 7).

boundary_rationale: The row is bounded to the single ha-davar header verse: הַדָּבָר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר חָזָ֔ה (oshb:Isa.2.1, byte tier), “This is what Isaiah the son of Amoz saw concerning Judah and Jerusalem.” (web:Isa.2.1). Unlike the chazon header at 1:1, this header opens with the noun ‘the word’ (ha-davar) rather than ‘the vision’ (chazon), a distinct header-noun class naming the same seer and Judah/Jerusalem object; it carries no imperative or address of its own, and verse 2 opens a fresh eschatological formula (“It shall happen in the latter days”, web:Isa.2.2), which is the row's own seam. Immediately upstream of that seam, 1:31 closes with a setumah break of its own (oshb:Isa.1.31, single-witness, tier-3), corroborating the division from the chapter that precedes it.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Folding 2:1 into the following mountain-of-the-house oracle was rejected because the header verse names no imperative or eschatological content of its own, unlike the material that follows it.

device_notes: The header-noun contrast with 1:1 (davar vs. chazon) is a genuine lexical distinction, not a copying variant. The two superscriptions also share three recurring elements at three different tiers: the relative clause אֲשֶׁ֣ר חָזָ֔ה collates at byte tier (oshb:Isa.1.1 tokens 5-6; oshb:Isa.2.1 tokens 2-3), the strongest of the three; the seer's name יְשַֽׁעְיָ֣הוּ / יְשַֽׁעְיָ֖הוּ collates at accent_stripped tier (oshb:Isa.1.1 token 2; oshb:Isa.2.1 token 4); and the patronymic בֶן אָמ֔וֹץ / בֶּן אָמ֑וֹץ collates at skeleton tier only, the construct form's dagesh and the name's accent both differing (oshb:Isa.1.1 tokens 3-4; oshb:Isa.2.1 tokens 5-6).
